hints: Each of the three arcs is subtended by an angle of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ radians (from the equilateral triangle) with radius $r = 2$ cm.
Calculate the length of one arc: $s = r\theta = 2 \times \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2pi}{3}$.
Multiply by $3$ to find the perimeter of the coin.
walkthrough:
Identify the radius and central angle for each of the three circular arcs:
$$r = 2\text{ cm}, \qquad \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

Calculate the length of one arc:
$$s = r\theta = 2 \times \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

Multiply by $3$ to find the total perimeter of the coin:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 3 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 2\pi\text{ cm} \quad (\approx 6.28\text{ cm})$$

hints: Calculate the area of equilateral triangle $ABC$: $\frac{1}{2}(2^2)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$.
Calculate the area of one circular sector: $\frac{1}{2}(2^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.
The area of one segment is $\text{Sector} - \triangle = \frac{2\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$.
The total area is $\text{Area of } \triangle + 3 \times \text{Segment Area}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the central equilateral triangle $ABC$ with side $2\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2}(2)(2)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3}$$

Calculate the area of one circular sector of radius $2\text{ cm}$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Area of sector} = \frac{1}{2}(2^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

Determine the area of one outer segment attached to each side of the triangle:
$$\text{Area of segment} = \text{Sector Area} - \text{Area of } \triangle ABC = \frac{2\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$$

Sum the triangle area and the three segment areas to find the total face area:
$$\text{Total Area} = \sqrt{3} + 3\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}\right) = \sqrt{3} + 2\pi - 3\sqrt{3} = 2\pi - 2\sqrt{3} = 2(\pi - \sqrt{3})$$
